transcript: Would you rather gain 500 or lose 500? Easy question, until both leave you with exactly the same money. Imagine you're given 1,000, then gain 500. Now imagine you're given 2,000, then lose 500. Both finish at 1,500. But the starting point changes the story. In a classic study, people choosing between a sure outcome and a gamble made different choices when equivalent final outcomes were framed as gains or losses. This is reference dependence. We evaluate changes against a starting point, not just the total. Your calculator sees the same answer. Your brain has hired two different headline writers. That doesn't mean everyone reacts identically or that losses always hurt exactly twice as much. Before judging a deal, write down the final amounts, the probabilities, and any real costs. Then compare those, not just the words gain and lose. A different headline isn't automatically a different deal.
normalization_note: Explicit500/1000/1500/2000 numeral-versus-written-number equivalence applied to BOTH texts; original raw mismatch preserved. Not an exact raw word match.
